_note: B-33. MailboxOps write levers (PowerShell, offline mock mailbox state; no Exchange Online is called). All R2 per the work inventory (W-M365-01, W-M365-02, W-M365-09, W-ONB-09, W-ONB-10). External forwarding is deliberately not a lever (W-M365-05 flags it). Exchange cmdlet names in the module are UNVERIFIED stand-ins; see levers/powershell/MailboxOps/SOURCES.md.

levers.name: mailbox.add-dl-member
levers.description: Add one person's mailbox to a distribution list of the client. Mock of an Exchange Online distribution group membership change.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

list.description: Primary address of the distribution list, e.g. frontdesk@contosodental.example

impact.L1: A new starter or a person who moved gets the group's mail from day one; a wrong list means they read mail meant for others, so the list is named in the approval.
impact.L2: The client's front desk or team address reaches the right people; adding someone to the wrong list can expose a team's mail to them.
impact.L3: A request technicians do many times a month becomes a checked, approved and audited change, one list and one person at a time.
impact.L4: The list must belong to the same client as the person; a list or person of another client is answered as not found, so no office's list is touched for another's.

levers.name: mailbox.remove-dl-member
levers.description: Remove one person's mailbox from a distribution list of the client. Undo of mailbox.add-dl-member.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

list.description: Primary address of the distribution list

impact.L1: A leaver or a person who moved stops getting a team's mail; removing the wrong person means they miss mail they need.
impact.L2: The client's group addresses stay accurate after people leave or move, so private team mail does not keep going to someone who changed roles.
impact.L3: Cleanup after a leaver is one approved, audited change instead of an edit nobody records.
impact.L4: Same-client list and person only; nothing outside the client's own lists can be changed.

levers.name: mailbox.grant-full-access
levers.description: Give one named person of the client Full Access to a mailbox. Mock of an Exchange Online mailbox permission grant.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

delegate.description: The person of the same client who gets Full Access

impact.L1: A shared or leaver's mailbox is opened by the one person who needs it, not by whoever asks; the delegate is named in the approval and a mailbox holds private mail, so a wrong grant exposes it.
impact.L2: A manager can cover a leaver's mail without the client sharing a password; a grant to the wrong person exposes confidential or regulated mail.
impact.L3: Every access grant to a mailbox is a registered, approved and audited change with an undo, which an auditor can ask to see.
impact.L4: The delegate must be a user of the same client; a person of another client or an outside address cannot be named.

levers.name: mailbox.revoke-full-access
levers.description: Remove one person's Full Access to a mailbox of the client. Undo of mailbox.grant-full-access.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

delegate.description: The person of the same client whose Full Access ends

impact.L1: Access that was only needed for a hand-over ends when the hand-over does; removing the wrong person stops someone doing their job.
impact.L2: Temporary access does not quietly become permanent, which is how mailbox access spreads in small offices.
impact.L3: Ending access is as controlled as granting it: approved, audited and convergent.

levers.name: mailbox.grant-send-as
levers.description: Let one named person of the client send mail as a mailbox. Mock of an Exchange Online Send As grant.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

delegate.description: The person of the same client who may send as this mailbox

impact.L1: A colleague can answer from a shared address such as info@ without a password; a wrong grant lets someone send mail that looks like it came from another person.
impact.L2: Mail from the practice's shared address comes from the right people; a wrong grant is a way to send believable mail in someone else's name.
impact.L3: Send As is a registered, approved and audited change with an undo and a dry-run diff.
impact.L4: Same-client delegate only; an outside address cannot be named.

levers.name: mailbox.revoke-send-as
levers.description: Remove one person's right to send as a mailbox of the client. Undo of mailbox.grant-send-as.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

delegate.description: The person of the same client whose Send As ends

impact.L1: Someone who changed roles can no longer send in another person's name; removing the wrong person stops them answering from a shared address.
impact.L2: Send As rights do not outlive the need for them.
impact.L3: Ending a Send As right is approved and audited like granting it.

levers.name: mailbox.convert-shared
levers.description: Convert a user mailbox of the client to a shared mailbox, so a leaver's mail is kept without a licence. Mock of an Exchange Online mailbox type change.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

impact.L1: A leaver's mail is kept for the people who need it and the account can be closed; done too early, the person loses sign-in to their mailbox. Over 50 GB is refused (limit UNVERIFIED).
impact.L2: The client stops paying for a leaver's licence without losing the mail, and an oversized mailbox is stopped for a licence decision instead of failing later.
impact.L3: A step technicians do by hand in every offboarding becomes one approved, audited change; there is no automated undo because converting back needs a licence.
impact.L4: Same-client mailbox only; the lever does not touch forwarding, litigation hold or retention, which stay with people.

levers.name: mailbox.set-auto-reply
levers.description: Turn on an automatic reply with the same text inside and outside the client for one mailbox. Mock of an Exchange Online auto-reply setting.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

message.description: The reply text: letters, digits and basic punctuation only, no links or markup

impact.L1: People who write to a leaver hear who to contact instead of waiting; the text goes to outside senders, so it is plain text with no links and the approver reads it.
impact.L2: Customers and vendors of the client are told whom to contact the day a person leaves.
impact.L3: The reply text is checked against a safe pattern and approved, so an auto-reply cannot carry a link or markup.
impact.L4: One mailbox of the client; no forwarding is set, only a reply.

levers.name: mailbox.clear-auto-reply
levers.description: Turn off the automatic reply on one mailbox of the client. Undo of mailbox.set-auto-reply.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

impact.L1: An out-of-date reply stops going to everyone who writes; turning it off too early means senders hear nothing.
impact.L2: A reply about a leaver does not stay on for years after the mailbox has a new owner.
impact.L3: Ending an auto-reply is approved and audited like setting one.

levers.name: mailbox.enable-archive
levers.description: Switch on the online archive for one mailbox of the client. Mock of an Exchange Online archive enablement.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

impact.L1: A person whose mailbox is full can keep working; enabling an archive is quiet but turning it off later can delete mail, so no undo lever is offered.
impact.L2: Full mailboxes stop bouncing client mail; the larger mailbox may need a licence level the client already pays for (UNVERIFIED).
impact.L3: A routine size fix becomes an approved, audited change instead of an unrecorded click.
impact.L4: One mailbox of the client; no content is moved or deleted.

levers.name: mailbox.grant-onedrive-manager
levers.description: Give a named manager of the client access to a leaver's OneDrive until a date within 30 days. Mock of a SharePoint Online site administrator grant.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

manager.description: The manager of the same client who gets access to the OneDrive

expires_on.description: Last day of the access as YYYY-MM-DD, after today and at most 30 days away

impact.L1: A manager can collect the files the team needs from a leaver within a set time instead of getting access for good; a wrong person or a long date means more people can read personal and client files.
impact.L2: Files are not lost when the account is closed, and the manager's access has an end date the approver sees.
impact.L3: The end date is part of what the approver signs. Nothing here removes the access on that date by itself; the revoke lever does, and a person or scheduled job must run it.
impact.L4: Same-client owner and manager only, at most 30 days, and no other file permission is changed.

levers.name: mailbox.revoke-onedrive-manager
levers.description: End a manager's access to a leaver's OneDrive. Undo of mailbox.grant-onedrive-manager, and what ends a grant on its date.

upn.description: userPrincipalName or primary address of the mailbox the change is about

manager.description: The manager of the same client whose access ends

impact.L1: A manager's access to a leaver's files ends when the hand-over does; ending it too early stops the files being copied.
impact.L2: Access to client and personal files does not stay open after the hand-over.
impact.L3: Ending a grant is approved and audited, so an auditor can see every grant had an end.
